imagePrompt: A teen golfer prepares to tee off with two tee-markers clearly set in their original position, unmoved.
imageAlt: A teen golfer on the teeing ground with unmoved tee-markers.

imageVerification.repairPrompt: No significant issues. If improvement is needed, ensure both tee-markers are perfectly identical in size and color, and the club grip detail is visible for added realism.

questions.title: Can you move the tee-markers?
questions.question: Are you allowed to move the tee-markers to get a better spot before you hit your first shot?

choices.text: Yes, you can move them and it’s not a problem.
No, if you move them to help yourself, you get a two-shot penalty.
Only if everyone playing says it’s okay.
Yes, but only if it’s raining.

questions.explanation: You are not allowed to move the tee-markers to help yourself get a better place to hit from. If you do, you get a two-stroke penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The two markers on the ground that show where you need to start playing each hole.
Extra shots added to your score if you break the rules.

questions.teachingTip: Let juniors walk up and point at the tee-markers on the ground, then explain that they show where you have to start. Remind them these cannot be moved to make the first shot easier.
likelyMisconceptions: Some children might think it’s okay to move tee-markers if the ground is muddy or if everyone agrees.
They may believe tee-markers are just decorations and can be moved out of the way.

questions.title: Moving the tee-markers
questions.question: Is it allowed to move the tee-markers to improve your position before teeing off?

choices.text: Yes, there is no penalty for moving them.
No, moving them to gain an advantage results in a two stroke penalty.
Yes, but only if it is raining.

questions.explanation: You must not move the tee-markers to improve your position. If you do, you receive a two-stroke penalty in stroke play.
